A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same multi-reference KL-regularized RLHF work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–H support reliable comparison despite the revised title, formatting, and added checklist.

before.justification: V2 reports original GRPO experiments on GSM8K and offline preference-optimization experiments on UltraFeedback, with results in Figure 1 and experimental details in Appendix H.

after.justification: V3 retains those experiments and adds a Qwen 2.5 7B UltraFeedback experiment with a 14B reference and GPT-4o win-rate evaluation in Table 2.

M1.justification: The RKL geometric aggregation, FKL arithmetic mixture, reward fitting, and Algorithms 1–2 are unchanged. The DPO objectives move from Appendix F, equations (60)–(61), to Section 7, equations (22)–(23). The larger-model experiment applies the existing method.

E1.justification: Both versions use GSM8K for mathematical reasoning and UltraFeedback for preference alignment. The additional 7B experiment retains the UltraFeedback data and task; model scale and judging procedures change under E3.

E2.justification: The original Figure 1 comparisons, including MRPO, are retained. New Table 2 adds comparisons against the base 7B model, its SFT stage, and DPO using either the SFT model or the 14B model as its sole reference.

E3.justification: Section 8 adds a protocol using a 7B policy, a 14B Instruct reference, SFT before DPO, and alpha = 0.5, evaluated by GPT-4o win rate against preferred UltraFeedback answers. Existing small-model experiments, metrics, and Appendix H splits remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Table 2 adds a limited larger-model check of reference composition: both references are compared with each reference alone, alongside base and SFT controls. The original reference-weight sweeps in Figure 1 are unchanged.

E5.justification: Figure 1 and Appendix H retain the three-seed, 95% confidence-interval reporting. However, new Table 2 reports only point estimates, despite the added checklist stating that all experiments include 95% intervals. No explicit increase in repeated runs is reported.

E6.justification: V3 adds Table 2 win rates: base model 8.6%, SFT 43.4%, DPO with the SFT reference 56.4%, DPO with the 14B reference 59.8%, and both-reference DPO 66.1%. Figure 1 is unchanged. These are additional results under a new configuration and metric, not improvements to earlier scores.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, assumptions, main bounds, and appendix proofs are retained. DPO equations are relocated and renumbered. Minor notation corrections and describing the existing FKL solution as implicit do not change the formal results or reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the claims of an exact multi-reference RKL solution, an FKL extension, and sample-complexity guarantees. The conclusion preserves the same comparison of optimality and sub-optimality rates.

C2.justification: V3 interprets the new experiment as validation at larger model scale. Section 9 also adds future directions addressing model misspecification through doubly robust optimization and extending inference-time algorithms. Existing bounded-reward limitations, coverage caveats, and RKL/FKL interpretations are retained.

D1.justification: Appendix H replaces the anonymous code-access link with a GitHub project link. Section 8 documents the larger-model identities, SFT stage, judge, and fixed reference weight. Existing hyperparameter searches, hardware descriptions, and computational-overhead information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V3 adds Xu et al. (2025) on doubly robust alignment and Mroueh (2024), Beirami et al. (2024), and Aminian et al. (2025) for inference-time extensions. These support added future directions; the central positioning against MRPO and prior RLHF theory remains unchanged.

P1.justification: V3 revises the title, corrects local wording, removes the contents page, and adds the conference checklist. It moves the DPO objectives and reward-bound/coverage discussion from Appendices F/G into Section 7. Most prose and the main section sequence are retained.

P2.justification: V3 adopts a substantially different conference layout throughout, including a redesigned title/author block, different typography and margins, and reflowed equations and paragraphs. Figure 1 and Table 1 are resized and repositioned, and Table 2 is added. The original plot content is retained.

improvement.justification: The 7B/14B experiment extends v2's small-model validation and tests both single-reference alternatives, providing useful additional support for practical applicability. Moving the DPO objectives into Section 7 improves accessibility. The gain remains limited: the theory is unchanged, the new experiment uses only alpha = 0.5, and Table 2 lacks confidence intervals despite the checklist's assertion.
